content:
Following on from the HeytingAlgebra (Subobject Y) thread (link, now PR #39618), a question that came out of the same work and that I'd appreciate a sanity check on.

The structure I'm using:

structure DistinctionStructure (C : Type*) [Category C] where

D : C ⥤ C

η : 𝟭 C ⟶ D

ι : D ⋙ D ≅ D

coherent : ∀ X, η.app (D.obj X) ≫ ι.hom.app X = 𝟙 (D.obj X)

Setting µ := ι.hom this is the left unit law of a monad plus µ iso. The full idempotent-monad structure would additionally require

  • right unit: D.map (η.app X) ≫ µ.app X = 𝟙 (D.obj X)
  • associativity: D.map (µ.app X) ≫ µ.app X = µ.app (D.obj X) ≫ µ.app X

Are these implied by the four fields above, or is DistinctionStructure genuinely weaker than "idempotent monad"?

My calculation says weaker. Using µ iso and the left unit to identify η.app (D.obj X) = µ.inv.app X, the right unit reduces to D.map (µ.hom.app X) = µ.hom.app (D.obj X). I don't see how this follows from ι being a natural transformation — naturality gives us squares parametrised by morphisms of C, but µ.hom.app (D.obj X) is indexed by an object that itself sits in the image of D, and the equation seems to reach outside what naturality covers.

But I've been wrong about this kind of thing before and would rather get a topos-theory sanity check than commit to "strictly weaker" in print without one. If the missing laws do follow, I can tighten the relevant remark. If they don't, is there a standard name for this structure (Karoubi-type splitting? split coreflection?) I should be citing.

Preprint context, in case it helps: https://github.com/thefalsework/papers/blob/main/preprints/four-position-partition/paper.md

The question above is essentially "should Remark 5.5 of this paper say ≡ or ⊊?".

Thanks.
